solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shift without cover in cold spell lately in club

indicators.note: in places the trimmed shift between the cold and spell letters

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: lately points to the end of the word spell, its final letter
losing its cover means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move slightly

explanation.surface: A weather report: something moved without shelter during a recent cold snap at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' tempts as a period of weather, but only its last letter is used; 'club' is the weapon, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon, a kind of club.

clue.text: Festive joke is usually kept by this very fine type

definitions.text: Festive joke is usually kept by this
definitions.meaning: a Christmas ... holds a paper joke inside
an excellent person or thing is informally a ...

explanation.surface: Where a Christmas joke lives, and a splendid sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British party tube that pops when pulled, holding a joke and paper hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive tube holds a joke, and in British slang something excellent is called a cracker.

clue.text: Dishonest practices in professional waste disposal?

definitions.meaning: clearing rubbish is literally filthy labour

explanation.surface: Corruption in the rubbish collection business.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names underhand deeds, while literally it is grubby toil like refuse collection.

clue.text: Film studio employee tried desperately to capture Oscar

indicators.note: to capture means the jumbled letters enclose the O
desperately suggests the letters of tried thrown wildly about

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A film worker tried hard to win an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award but is the radio-alphabet O; 'desperately' gives TRIED rearranged, around O.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor cuts and assembles footage, a typical job at a film studio.

clue.text: Secure title for letter?

definitions.note: read as one who lets, a letter is someone renting out property

parts.note: to land a deal or a fish is to secure it
Lord is a noble title

explanation.surface: A question about what heading to give a written letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is read not as correspondence but as one who lets property; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets out a house or room to tenants is its owner, so 'one who lets' is a playful description.

clue.text: Leading flier conceals hard pain

indicators.note: conceals means the pilot word hides the letter inside

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A top pilot hides a severe pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain.

clue.text: Ignore reduction by a retailer

definitions.meaning: to dismiss or disregard as unimportant
a price cut offered in a shop

explanation.surface: Disregard a shop's price cut.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means disregard; as a noun, a lower price a shop charges.

clue.text: Top number recalled as potential tearjerker?

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, means the letters are taken in reverse order

parts.note: the top one is number one, written NO 1

explanation.surface: A leading song brought back as a weepie.
explanation.walkthrough: NO 1 (number one, with I as 1) plus NO, reading upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable makes your eyes water, a playful sense of something that makes you cry.

clue.text: See director after money, reportedly, being guileless

indicators.note: after puts the seeing and director part following the money part
reportedly means the word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: dough is slang for money
to eye is to see or look at

explanation.surface: A film director meets financiers and seems naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns DOUGH into DOE, a word with the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Doe-eyed means having large innocent eyes, hence naive and lacking cunning.

clue.text: Australian following onslaught is frightened

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a raid is a sudden attack or onslaught

explanation.surface: An Australian is scared after coming under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a position word but supplies the abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scared or fearful is a direct synonym of being frightened.

clue.text: This case is reviewed for discipline

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of this case are looked at again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A legal or school case is being looked at again before punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' is the anagram signal for the eight letters of THIS CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone is to punish or rebuke them severely, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Stock place in middle of hotels for block

indicators.note: in places the farm word inside those central letters
middle of takes the central letters of hotels

parts.note: a ranch is where livestock are raised

explanation.surface: A cattle farm set among hotels as a building plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shares, which fits the definition, but here it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or block, especially of shares or money.

clue.text: Device for securing strip of wood in musical instrument

parts.note: a key secures a lock
a board is a flat strip or plank of wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter fixing a wooden strip inside a piano or similar instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic keyboard is a musical instrument played with keys like a piano.

clue.text: Lad embracing pursuit in East London gets reward

indicators.note: embracing means the lad's word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a hunt is a pursuit; Cockney speech of East London drops the H, giving 'unt

explanation.surface: A young man from the East End is chased and paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the East London accent, drops initial H, so 'hunt' becomes 'unt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty is a sum paid as a reward, especially for capturing someone.

clue.text: English master getting cross in Dubai, perhaps

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA
cross means angry, irate

explanation.surface: An English schoolmaster gets annoyed in Dubai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' supplies only M; EMIR is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven states of the United Arab Emirates, a realm ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Course announced in beginning

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: a route is a course taken from one place to another

explanation.surface: A course of action declared at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'route' rhymes with 'boot', so it sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its origin or source, where it begins.

clue.text: Single operator supported by staff and airline in aim

parts.note: something supported by another rests on it

indicators.note: in puts the staff and airline letters inside the aim

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
to staff a post is to man it
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: A sole trader backed by employees and a carrier with an objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' looks like a link but gives ON, as in resting on something; 'and' here is a mere joiner between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band is a person who runs a business or does a job entirely alone, without help.

clue.text: A friend keeps pairs prepared for evaluation

indicators.note: keeps means the outer words hold the jumbled letters

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters of pairs made up into a new form

explanation.surface: A friend keeps pairs ready for an assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment of worth or performance.

clue.text: British colleague, hilarious sort caught short in fuss

parts.note: an ally is an associate or colleague

indicators.note: caught short means the word is cut off at its end

parts.note: a hoot is a very funny person

explanation.surface: A British workmate and a joker caught out in a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught short' is British slang for urgently needing a toilet, here used to trim HOOT to HOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy publicity or a big commotion.

clue.text: Perfectly describing mascot's role?

definitions.meaning: a mascot acts as a lucky charm, so its role is to be like one

explanation.surface: Perfectly describing what a mascot is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Working like a charm is an idiom for going perfectly; a mascot is literally a lucky charm.

clue.text: Run lady arranged for household task?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of run lady are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman organising housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing the washing of clothes is a typical household chore.

clue.text: Sail in resort by river

definitions.note: a sail is borne on a spar, the clue naming the whole rig by its part

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Going sailing at a riverside holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the river after the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a pole of a ship's rigging that carries canvas, standing loosely for it.

clue.text: Sign to stop mate going wild for beef, say

parts.note: a red traffic light means stop

indicators.note: going wild suggests the letters of mate running riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A red signal and a mate losing control over beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' hints at a complaint, but is the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is an example of the dark meat from cattle, lamb or venison.

clue.text: Silky wool has note in Greek marketplace

indicators.note: in places the note inside the Greek marketplace

parts.note: the agora was a public market place in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Fine fabric with a price tag in a Greek market.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is soft wool from Angora goats or rabbits.

clue.text: Rowdy rugby lot's leader enters a French yard

indicators.note: enters means the rugby letters go inside the French and yard letters

parts.note: un is French for a
RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of lot's

explanation.surface: A noisy rugby crowd's captain walks into a French yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly behaviour is disorderly and rowdy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Speedy type found in disgrace repeatedly

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie inside the run of words disgrace repeatedly

explanation.surface: A fast person keeps getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a person or machine that runs in races, someone fast.

clue.text: Put up with character losing head? That's normal

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a card is an eccentric character

explanation.surface: Tolerating an odd person is presented as typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means an eccentric, CARD, which losing its head gives ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual or typical, matching normal as an adjective.

clue.text: Measure of speed in strike that's mounted

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means the word reads upward

parts.note: tonk is British slang for hit hard

explanation.surface: Measuring how fast a blow lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is one nautical mile per hour, a unit of speed.

clue.text: Cover part of a watch for ordinary sailor

parts.note: to deck something is to cover or adorn it
a hand is a pointer on a watch face

explanation.surface: A sailor covering a watch shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' hints at a ship's duty period, but it is the timepiece with hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member doing manual work on deck, a lowly seaman.

clue.text: Jerry, maybe, acquires special hair lotion

indicators.note: acquires means the mouse takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Jerry of Tom and Jerry cartoons is a mouse

explanation.surface: A man named Jerry buys a special hair product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry' looks like a person but is the cartoon mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousse is a foamy styling product applied to hair.

clue.text: Teenager waylays a marine in Isle of Wight town

indicators.note: waylays means the teenager catches and holds the others within

parts.note: a youth is a teenager
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A young thug ambushes a soldier in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarmouth is a small port town on the Isle of Wight's west side.

clue.text: Largely uncovered a great deal in vote

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: bald means bare or uncovered
a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: A mostly open vote counts heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a secret vote or the process of voting.
